chunks: And with this chain of narration - from Yunus from Ziyad ibn Marwan who said:
I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about completing the prayer in the two Sanctuaries, so he said, 'I like for you what I like for myself: complete the prayer.'

key_terms.أَبَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ: Abu Ibrahim (a title for Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِتْمَامِ: Completing the prayer (performing four rak'ahs instead of two)
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Sanctuaries (referring to Mecca and Medina)

ai.seo_question: Should pilgrims shorten their prayers in Mecca and Medina?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Ziyad ibn Marwan inquires of Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding the validity of shortening prayers (Qasr) versus performing full prayers (Tamam) while in the two Sanctuaries. The Imam’s response, 'I like for you what I like for myself,' establishes a strong preference for performing full four-rak'ah prayers, aligning with the view that the status of a resident (Muqim) in Mecca and Medina supersedes the traveler's status for the purpose of prayer length. This reflects the broader Shia juristic discussion on whether the sanctity of the location or the duration of stay determines the ruling, emphasizing the Imam's personal practice as a normative guide.
